question: The difference between two numbers is 18 & their product is 63. What is the square of their sum?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

⇒ Use identity: (a + b)² = (a − b)² + 4ab

⇒ Given: a − b = 18, ab = 63

⇒ (a + b)² = 18² + 4 × 63

⇒ = 324 + 252 = 576

**∴ Answer = 576**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Difference of two numbers = 18

Product = 63

**Formula Used:**

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

(a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab

**Calculation:**

⇒ (a − b)² = 18² = 324

⇒ (a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab

⇒ 324 = a² + b² − 2(63)

⇒ 324 = a² + b² − 126

⇒ a² + b² = 450

⇒ (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

⇒ = 450 + 2(63)

⇒ = 450 + 126 = 576

**∴ Final Answer = 576**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**Key Identity:** (a + b)² = (a − b)² + 4ab

**Algebra Trick:** Use identities to avoid finding numbers

**Symmetry:** Sum and difference relations simplify problems

**Exam Tip:** Always check if identity-based shortcut applies
